skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Routes video-edit requests to the appropriate RunComfy model for restyling, background changes, motion transfer, outfit swaps, and packaging edits. It provides model-specific prompt patterns and CLI invocation guidance for Wan 2.7, Kling 2.6 Pro, and Lucy Edit Restyle.
skill.summary: Route video edit requests to the right RunComfy model with focused prompt guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown syntax, inline parameter names, placeholder URLs, or documented model IDs rather than executable code. Confirmed risk remains where the skill instructs agents to install or run the RunComfy CLI, submit media and prompts to a third-party service, download outputs, and use token-based authentication. No prompt injection attempt or hidden malicious instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before installing or running RunComfy CLI commands, and show the exact command and output directory.
Add a clear consent step before submitting prompts, media URLs, or reference assets to RunComfy services.
Recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for temporary environments and document how to revoke tokens and protect ~/.config/runcomfy/token.json.
Replace https://... examples and <absolute/path> placeholders with safer sample values that avoid traversal-like patterns.

content.value_statement: Choosing the right RunComfy video model is difficult when edits need identity, motion, or background control. This skill routes each request to the best model and supplies focused prompt patterns.
actual_capabilities: Classifies a video edit request into restyle, background, packaging, motion transfer, or outfit swap routes.
Selects Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, or Lucy Edit Restyle.
Builds model-specific prompt guidance for identity, pose, motion, framing, lip movement, and audio preservation.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns with JSON inputs for each supported model.
Documents practical limits for duration, resolution, source media, and model-specific controls.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and either login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.
Processes media through RunComfy services, so users must avoid private or unauthorized content.
Routes one model per request and does not blend outputs across models.
Final quality depends on source video length, resolution, composition, and model behavior.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Clips
use_cases.description: Swap backgrounds, packaging designs, or lighting while preserving product framing and camera motion.

use_cases.title: Transfer Character Motion
use_cases.description: Apply motion from a reference clip to a target character for quick concept variations.

use_cases.title: Restyle Short Videos
use_cases.description: Change outfits, atmosphere, or visual style while keeping face, pose, and movement stable.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Background Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple background change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this video: {video_url}. Preserve the speaker face, pose, lip movement, and audio. Change the background to {background_style}.

prompt_templates.title: Outfit Restyle
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a localized identity-stable edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle {video_url}. Preserve face and motion. Change the outfit to {outfit_description}. Use Lucy when this is a localized edit.

prompt_templates.title: Motion Transfer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that uses a motion reference clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use {motion_reference_video} to drive the motion of {target_character_image}. Keep identity stable and preserve the reference audio when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Route And Optimize
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning request before running a model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best RunComfy route for {goal}. Explain the selected model, required media, prompt priorities, and known limits before running it.

output_examples.input: Restyle a walking portrait video with business attire and keep identity stable.
output_examples.output: The skill routes to Lucy Edit Restyle, prioritizes face and motion preservation, and requests a localized outfit change.

output_examples.input: Move a character like the dancer in my reference clip.
output_examples.output: The skill routes to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control and treats the video as the motion reference.

output_examples.input: Change a product demo background and keep the camera movement.
output_examples.output: The skill routes to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video and asks for background replacement with framing and motion preservation.

best_practices: Use one edit direction per run so the model can preserve motion and identity.
Place preservation goals first, including face, pose, framing, lip movement, or audio.
Use reference images only when the edit needs direct visual transfer.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated edits, such as outfit, background, and camera changes in one request.
Do not submit private media or unlicensed content to third-party processing services.
Do not use placeholder paths or URLs when running a real edit.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It routes video edit requests to supported RunComfy models and gives model-specific prompt guidance.

faq.question: Which models does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, and Lucy Edit Restyle.

faq.question: Does it edit files locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI, which submits work to RunComfy services and downloads generated outputs.

faq.question: What input media does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects short video URLs and optional reference images or motion clips, depending on the selected route.

faq.question: Can it preserve identity and audio?
faq.answer: It prompts for identity, motion, framing, lip movement, and original audio preservation when supported.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive media?
faq.answer: Use caution. Media URLs, prompts, and outputs are processed by RunComfy and should not include confidential content.
